title: Clifford completeness of the 16 Dirac matrices as a Fierz reconstruction
expression_sketch: Dirac spinor indices alpha,beta,gamma,delta in {1,2,3,4}. Lorentz indices mu,nu in {0,1,2,3}. Minkowski metric eta = diag(+1,-1,-1,-1). Gamma matrices satisfy {gamma^mu, gamma^nu} = 2*eta^{mu nu}*I_4. Standard 16-element basis of M_4(C) (Wikipedia Fierz identity; Itzykson--Zuber): Gamma^A in { I_4, gamma^mu, sigma^{mu nu} for mu<nu, gamma^5 gamma^mu, gamma^5 } with sigma^{mu nu} = (I/2)*[gamma^mu, gamma^nu] and gamma^5 = I*gamma^0*gamma^1*gamma^2*gamma^3. Trace orthonormality: Tr(Gamma^A * Gamma_A') = 4 * delta^{A A'} after lowering A with the bilinear that makes the basis orthogonal (signs from eta on vector and tensor sectors). Completeness / reconstruction of the index-swap operator: (1/4)*Sum_A Gamma^A(alpha,beta)*Gamma_A(gamma,delta) == delta(alpha,delta)*delta(beta,gamma). Equivalent expansion of an arbitrary 4x4 matrix M: M = (1/4)*Sum_A Tr(M*Gamma_A)*Gamma^A. Chiral Fierz table (Wikipedia): the 5x5 rearrangement of (bar chi Gamma^A psi)(bar psi' Gamma_A chi') into S,V,T,A,P bilinears is the same completeness contracted on spinors.
latent_structure: Hilbert--Schmidt basis reconstruction of M_4(C) from the Clifford algebra Cl(1,3). The 16 Dirac generators play the role of TENSOR_GENERATOR / BASIS_OBJECT; completeness is BASIS_RECONSTRUCT of the swap operator on C^4 tensor C^4. Distinct from su(2) Pauli completeness (2x2, four matrices including identity, no Clifford grading).

function_domains.gamma: Dirac matrices generating Cl(1,3) with {gamma^mu, gamma^nu}=2 eta^{mu nu} I_4, any fixed representation (Dirac, Weyl, or Majorana).
function_domains.gamma5: chirality matrix I*gamma^0 gamma^1 gamma^2 gamma^3, (gamma5)^2 = I_4, {gamma5, gamma^mu}=0.
function_domains.sigma: sigma^{mu nu} = (I/2)[gamma^mu, gamma^nu], six independent antisymmetric pairs mu<nu.
function_domains.Gamma_A: The ordered 16-matrix basis {I, gamma^mu, sigma^{mu nu} (mu<nu), gamma5 gamma^mu, gamma5}.

nonzero_conditions.statement: The scalar 4 = Tr(I_4) is invertible in Q, so the completeness prefactor 1/4 is defined.
nonzero_conditions.label: DECLARED
nonzero_conditions.source: Wikipedia Fierz identity, 4-dimensional Dirac completeness with coefficient 1/4; Itzykson--Zuber

branch_conventions: gamma5 uses the imaginary unit I as in the Minkowski product I gamma^0 gamma^1 gamma^2 gamma^3; this is an algebraic matrix, not a branched function.
source_provenance: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fierz_identity (Dirac bilinear completeness; S,V,T,A,P rearrangement table in 4D).
C. Itzykson and J.-B. Zuber, Quantum Field Theory, McGraw-Hill 1980, Appendix A-2 (Dirac algebra and Fierz).
M. E. Peskin and D. V. Schroeder, An Introduction to Quantum Field Theory, Addison-Wesley 1995, Appendix A.3.
J. F. Nieves and P. B. Pal, Generalized Fierz identities, Am. J. Phys. 72 (2004) 1100, arXiv:hep-ph/0306087.

derived_conditions.statement: The 16 matrices Gamma^A are linearly independent in the 16-dimensional space M_4(C), hence a basis; completeness is the component form of M = (1/4) Sum_A Tr(M Gamma_A) Gamma^A.
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Wikipedia Gamma matrices, identities / linear independence paragraph; Wikipedia Fierz identity

derived_conditions.statement: Any two representations of the Dirac algebra on C^4 are unitarily equivalent (up to the discrete inner-automorphism by gamma5 in 4D), so the completeness identity is representation-independent.
derived_conditions.label: DECLARED
derived_conditions.source: Wikipedia Gamma matrices, Pauli's fundamental theorem / representation theory paragraph

public_source: Wikipedia Fierz identity and Gamma matrices; Itzykson--Zuber Appendix A-2; Peskin--Schroeder Appendix A.3
why_not_cse_lgg: A sum of 16 Kronecker products of 4x4 components does not CSE into a combination of spinor-index Kroneckers. LGG has no Clifford-algebra constructor. Distinct from ac-t-pauli-completeness (2-component, three Pauli generators plus I).
proposer_leak_risk: Hide Fierz, Dirac, Clifford, gamma5, chiral, completeness. Show only the summed 4x4 bilinears in spinor indices.
notes: Finite matrix identity over C. Mostly-plus eta is declared; the completeness relation itself is a statement about M_4(C) and is insensitive to the mostly-plus versus mostly-minus convention once the dual basis Gamma_A is lowered consistently. Distinct from Pauli SU(2) Fierz.
